question: Can a target-free probability-measure transport from matched ASCENT B0 support to frozen C161 support, followed by a fixed Energy-KL proximal solve, recover NLL and Brier without altering C161 geometry or using a residual, learned gate, or calibration search?

hypotheses.primary: TPMO improves both NLL and Brier over native C161 in each frozen fold, reaches aggregate B0 non-inferiority, and retains C161 Energy within one percent.
hypotheses.mechanism: B0 supplies probability semantics, exact permutation marginalization aligns those semantics to the independently trained C161 support, and the Energy-KL proximal objective preserves C161 finite-measure quality.
rivals: B0 winner events do not transfer to C161 winner events even after support alignment.
The cross-support geometry is too ambiguous for a target-free assignment posterior.
The unit Energy-KL objective retains too much B0 prior mass or too much C161 Energy mass to pass both proper-score gates.
Any apparent actor-level gain is concentrated in a few calendar dates.
hypotheses.null: The fixed TPMO candidate fails at least one frozen gate and C162 closes without tuning, arm switching, training, development access, or locked-test access.

algorithm.name: TPMO
algorithm.source_measure: FP64 softmax of frozen matched C127 B0 logits
algorithm.assignment_posterior: softmax of negative mean normalized assignment cost with fixed unit inverse scale
algorithm.transport: exact marginalization of B0 probability mass over the 120 assignment posterior
algorithm.proximal_objective: C134 predicted Energy divided by ADE_SCALE plus KL(p || transported_prior)
algorithm.solver: batched equality-constrained Newton with deterministic Armijo backtracking
algorithm.top1_decision: unchanged frozen C161 C133 decision-regret argmin

stopping_rule: Evaluate the frozen TPMO main candidate once on folds 1 and 2. Any failed gate closes C162. Mechanism controls may diagnose failure but may not replace TPMO.
claim_boundary: C162 is a retrospectively designed train-date screen on folds already used to establish C161. Passing would support a local mechanism result only; a new sealed event or compatible external dataset is required for a confirmatory generalization claim.
